title: No cure for Czech Republic productivity malaise in sight
gist: Oxford Economics cuts Czech long-run GDP growth to about 2% a year over the next decade (from 2.9% in 2000-2019) because productivity has stalled since 2019 and labour-supply tailwinds are fading.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics downgrades Czech long-term GDP growth to an average 2% over the next decade versus 2.9% in 2000-2019, because output per hour worked has effectively stalled since 2019.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Lower Czech potential growth weighs on long-run assets and convergence stories.

insights.claim: Czech growth has relied on labour supply, notably about 400,000 Ukrainian refugees and rising participation, which is unsustainable given low fertility and an ageing population.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Demographic headwinds will bite as labour inflows end.

insights.claim: ICT and high-end manufacturing are bright spots but have not lifted the broader economy, and the government's industrial strategy identifies the issues but lacks funding and prioritises other areas.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
